title: How Bryan Johnson achieved a 100% sleep score: six rules for reliably great sleep
summary: Bryan explains how he reached eight months of perfect sleep scores by treating sleep as a top priority. He covers meal timing, light exposure, wind-down routines, consistent bedtimes and managing caffeine.

principles.text: Treat sleep with the same seriousness and devotion as work; build your life around it.
principles.quote: You need to treat sleep with the same level of seriousness and devotion as you do your work. It demands your best performance.

principles.text: Finish your last meal at least two hours before bed, gradually moving it earlier to lower resting heart rate.
principles.quote: If your bedtime is 10 PM, finish eating by 8 PM. Then day by day, move it back by 30 minutes.

principles.text: A lower resting heart rate at bedtime means better sleep.
principles.quote: The lower your resting heart rate, the better your sleep.

principles.text: Avoid blue light an hour or two before bed; use red and amber lights instead.
principles.quote: An hour or two before bed, try to avoid blue light. That means turn off screens, or eliminate blue light from your screens

principles.text: Create a wind-down routine that separates you from work and calms body and mind.
principles.quote: You can't just finish work and put your head on the pillow and expect great sleep. You need to calm your body and mind down.

principles.text: Keep bedtime consistent, within +/- 30 minutes every day, because the body rewards routine.
principles.quote: Go to bed within +/- 30 minutes of your chosen bedtime every single day. Create the habit and stay with the habit.
